In mathematics, '''Monk's formula''', found by {{harvtxt|Monk|1959}}, is an analogue of [[Pieri's formula]] that describes the product of a linear [[Schubert polynomial]] by a Schubert polynomial.  Equivalently, it describes the product of a special [[Schubert cycle]] by a Schubert cycle in the [[cohomology]] of a [[flag manifold]].

Write ''t''<sub>ij</sub> for the [[Transposition (mathematics)|transposition]] ''(i j)'', and ''s''<sub>i</sub> = ''t''<sub>i,i+1</sub>. Then 𝔖<sub>s<sub>r</sub></sub> = ''x''<sub>1</sub> + ⋯ + ''x''<sub>r</sub>, and Monk's formula states that for a permutation ''w'',

<math>
\mathfrak{S}_{s_r} \mathfrak{S}_w = \sum_{{i \leq r < j} \atop {\ell(wt_{ij}) = \ell(w)+1}} \mathfrak{S}_{wt_{ij}},
</math>

where <math>\ell(w)</math> is the [[length]] of ''w''. The pairs (''i'', ''j'') appearing in the sum are exactly those such that ''i'' &le; ''r'' < ''j'', ''w''<sub>i</sub> < ''w''<sub>j</sub>, and there is no ''i'' < ''k'' < ''j'' with ''w''<sub>i</sub> < ''w''<sub>k</sub> < ''w''<sub>j</sub>; each ''wt''<sub>ij</sub> is a cover of ''w'' in [[Bruhat order]].
